subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw first standardize only existing readiness observations as canonical conditions, or also accept the proposed hosting profiles, plugin-provider API, operator composition, and CLI now?
rationale: The proposal creates durable contracts across actively shared Gateway, plugin, configuration, CLI, and hosting boundaries; neither the draft implementation nor automated review can choose that permanent product boundary.

options.title: Accept conditions first
options.body: Approve canonical conditions and legacy-compatible projections, then decide profiles, providers, operator composition, and CLI separately.

options.title: Accept the full framework
options.body: Approve every proposed contract together after affected owners review semantics, upgrades, and packaged runtime proof.

options.title: Prefer targeted fixes
options.body: Address the active readiness failures narrowly and defer a generalized framework until operational demand is stronger.

recommendation.title: Accept conditions first
recommendation.body: Approve canonical conditions and legacy-compatible projections, then decide profiles, providers, operator composition, and CLI separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history shows the broadest overlap across the central plugin API and Gateway dependency surfaces, although the decision should include the other listed owners.
